end.summary:
Practised copying shapes on dot and square grids by counting units along sides.
Completed 7 attempts; 4 were correct without help.
Myra initially counted dots instead of gaps on a dot grid.
They later stated that three dots make two gaps and used this to correct the measurement.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Myra practised copying shapes by counting the gaps between dots and tracking each side’s direction and length. They corrected the dot-versus-gap mix-up later by explaining that three dots make two gaps, then applied the idea to describe a shape as 3 right and 2 down from the start. At home, draw two or three simple shapes on a dot grid and ask Myra to count the gaps along each side before copying them.
